digest.key_takeaway:
On November 19, 2026, Docker launched a new brand built around one message: "Run on Trust". The whale got a redesign, the website changed, and the story moved toward AI agents. A viral version of the news has been going around, and some of it is wrong. I care less about the logo than about what Docker Run on Trust says about AI agent security, because that is the problem platform, DevSecOps and SRE teams are being handed right now.

articles.title: NVIDIA GR00T 2 Teaches Robots a New Job From 5 Demonstrations: 95% Success, With One Big Asterisk
articles.summary: Teaching a robot a new job used to mean weeks of programming, or months of collecting robot training data. NVIDIA's GR00T 2, introduced on 9 November at the Conference on Robot Learning in Austin, claims to cut that down to an afternoon. Show it a task five times, fine-tune for about 30 minutes on a single RTX 5090 graphics card, and NVIDIA reports 95 percent average success across 50 dexterous tasks. articles.title: AWS Releases a Free Local Emulator of AWS Built Entirely by Agents
articles.summary: AWS has released AWS Emulator, a free, CC0-licensed local stand-in for more than 200 of its services, generated from its public API models and aimed at the test loops of coding agents. AWS says agents wrote and maintain all of the code and publishes per-release fidelity scores. The docs say it does not evaluate IAM, and practitioners are split on trusting an emulator nobody reviewed. By Steef-Jan Wiggers

articles.title: Google Donates Agent Substrate and gVisor to the CNCF to Secure AI Agents at Scale
articles.summary: Google has announced it is donating Agent Substrate and gVisor to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), placing two important components of its AI agent infrastructure under vendor-neutral open-source governance. By Craig Risi

articles.title: Anthropic IPO: what the prospectus says about rate limits and compute
articles.summary: Anthropic began trading on Nasdaq on Thursday, November 19, 2026 under the symbol ANT. The first trade was $111.50, the close was $97.17, and the final prospectus contains a sentence that matters to anyone who builds on Claude: the company says it has changed usage limits and rate limits before and may change them again. This article covers what the day-one numbers show, who was allowed to sell shares, what the Anthropic IPO prospectus says about rate limits and compute, and one contract in the filing that either side can already cancel. It accompanies today's Daily Diff episode.

articles.title: Stop the agent from switching the styling approach “while we’re here”
articles.summary:
The bug is a truncated label. The diff also rewrites the file from CSS Modules to Tailwind “so it matches the newer pages,” or from a styled component to a stack of inline styles “to keep it local.” The visual fix is one min-width. The rest is a styling migration with no design review.

I’ve started telling agents to keep the styling approach the file already uses. A bugfix is not the moment to introduce a second (or third) styling system in the same folder.

articles.title: There is no official Postgres MCP server. I compared the 37 that do exist.
articles.summary:
If you want an AI agent to talk to PostgreSQL, you open your client, go looking for "the Postgres MCP server", and hit the first surprise: there isn't one. Not an official one, anyway.

I run Serverdex, a directory synced daily from the official Model Context Protocol registry. As of 20 November 2026 the index holds 37 MCP servers whose name carries "Postgres". Zero of them are published by PostgreSQL or by a hosted-Postgres vendor. All 37 are community projects. So the real question is not "which is the official one" but "which of 37 community servers do I trust with my database".

articles.title: Top developer security best practices: building a controlled environment, stage by stage
articles.summary:
AI is changing the way developers work. Just a few years ago, they didn't have to think about security. The job was to write code, not to secure it.

But as teams have shrunk and code velocity has increased, security is now in the developer's purview. According to Aikido’s State of AI in Security & Development 2026 report, AI tools now write 24% of production code. Half of the respondents also believe they’d be blamed if AI-generated code they wrote introduced a vulnerability.

articles.title: 190MB to 60MB: PostgreSQL 19's REPACK ties VACUUM FULL
articles.summary:
190MB to 60MB: PostgreSQL 19's REPACK ties VACUUM FULL


PostgreSQL 19's new REPACK command shrank my bloated table from 199.8 MB to 59.9 MB in 471 ms — the same size, to the byte, in the same time as VACUUM FULL. The version that doesn't block writers took 590 ms and left 262,144 extra bytes behind. The feature is real. The speedup is not.

articles.title: .NET 11 : ASP.NET Core: Union Type Support, OpenAPI 3.2 by Default and Blazor AI Components

The update adds C# union type support in JSON bodies, asynchronous validation for Minimal APIs, OpenAPI 3.2 by default, and SignalR authentication refresh. Blazor gains a CacheView component, client-side validation for static SSR forms, opt-in circuit pause for inactive tabs, and experimental AI components. Zstandard compression is on by default. By Almir Vuk
